axes.xDefinition: log10 stellar mass (FAST, Bruzual & Charlot 2003, Salpeter IMF, delayed-exponential SFHs)
axes.yDefinition: log10 of the mode of the SFR distribution of star-forming galaxies, SFR = SFR_UV (uncorrected, Daddi+04) + SFR_IR (Kennicutt98), Salpeter IMF, from mean Herschel stacks corrected to the mode (about -0.1 dex)

representation.equation: log10 SFR_MS = m - m0 + a0 r - a1 [max(0, m - m1 - a2 r)]^2, m = log10(M*/1e9 Msun), r = log10(1+z) (Eq. 7)

scatter.meaning: non-varying dispersion of log SFR at fixed mass and redshift from scatter stacking (0.30 +-0.06 Herschel; 0.33 +-0.03 COSMOS UltraVISTA), not an uncertainty of the curve

selection.population: mass-complete star-forming galaxies selected with the UVJ criterion (U-V>1.3, V-J<1.6, U-V>0.88(V-J)+0.49 = quiescent), GOODS-N/S, UDS, COSMOS CANDELS H-band and GOODS-N/COSMOS UltraVISTA Ks-band catalogues
selection.warning: The fit was made to the filled circles of Fig. 8 (stacked mass/redshift bins with 0.3<z<5.0 in six redshift bins); the stacks span log M* = 9.74 to 11.21, so the expression is an extrapolation outside this mass range and outside 0.3<z<5.0. The paper's text says the catalogue is mass-complete above 2e10 Msun and extends to z=4. Abstract: flattening at log M* > 10.5. Quiescent galaxies, not AGN, are excluded.

provenance.citation: Schreiber et al. 2015, A&A 575, A74 (arXiv:1409.5433), Eq. 7

records.notes: Analytic redshift evolution (variable z in the expression). Verification: parameters parsed from the arXiv source; the expression, evaluated at the legend bin centres, reproduces the six grey best-fit curves of the paper's Fig. 8 with rms 0.007-0.016 dex and maximum 0.04 dex (digitisation of vector paths, axes calibrated on tick marks).

definitions.sfrIndicator: UV (uncorrected, 1500 A) + IR (Herschel stacks, CE01 templates), L_IR from 24-500 micron stacks
definitions.sfrTimescaleBasis: 'assume that the SFR remained constant over the last 100 Myr'
definitions.sfrStatisticBasis: 'in all the following we refer to the SFR of the main sequence as the mode of the distribution'
